title: Safe AI-Assisted Software Release with Behavioral Programming
shortDescription: Compare alternative AI-integration strategies, then integrate an AI defect-risk recommendation into a pull-request workflow using independently verifiable software guardrails.

courseAlignment.evidence: Investigate the use and limitations of AI defect-risk prediction within a software release workflow.
Compare AI-integration strategies, justify an appropriate architecture, and apply Behavioral Programming as the selected control method.
Interpret risk probability and confidence in context as preparation for later quantitative system evaluation and the Final Project.

learningOutcomes: Investigate the role and limitations of AI defect-risk prediction in a software-engineering release workflow.
Compare alternative AI-integration strategies using auditability, maintainability, safety, retraining dependence, and human-review requirements.
Justify and apply a separated AI-recommendation and deterministic-policy architecture using Behavioral Programming.
Implement explicit constraints for failed tests, security findings, confidence, and coverage without modifying the AI model.
Verify and critically interpret the behavior of the combined AI-enabled software workflow across multiple pull-request scenarios.

tasks.title: Compare the three AI-integration strategies
tasks.description: Before coding, compare direct AI authority, putting all rules inside the AI model, and separating AI prediction from deterministic software policy. Use auditability, maintainability, safety, retraining dependence, and human review as your criteria. Record a short justification in the report.

tasks.title: Run the AI-only baseline
tasks.description: Open main.py. Keep ENABLE_GUARDRAIL = False and ACTIVE_CASE = "PR-1042". Click Run Python. Do not change the code yet.

tasks.title: Read the baseline result
tasks.description: Record the AI risk label, risk probability, confidence, failed tests, security findings, and final decision. Identify why DEPLOY is not acceptable for this case.

tasks.title: Implement release_guardrail()
tasks.description: In main.py, complete only release_guardrail(change, prediction). Hard violations must block DEPLOY and request BLOCK_RELEASE. Low confidence or low coverage must require HUMAN_REVIEW.

tasks.title: Enable the guardrail and run again
tasks.description: Change ENABLE_GUARDRAIL to True. Run PR-1042 again. Confirm that the AI prediction stays the same but the final software decision changes appropriately.

tasks.title: Try the remaining pull-request cases
tasks.description: Run PR-1001, PR-1057, PR-1088, and PR-1093. For each case, distinguish the AI prediction from the final action allowed by the software workflow.

tasks.title: Verify the requirements
tasks.description: Click Verify Requirements. All checks should pass. If one fails, use its message to fix the policy logic rather than changing the AI model.

tasks.title: Complete and export the report
tasks.description: Explain your strategy choice, baseline, guardrail logic, scenario results, critical interpretation, and how this pattern could transfer to the Final Project. Export the report to Word.
